symptom: ako/mxcli#2043 (mendixlabs/mxcli#1780): `exec --no-check` of a large script panicked with a nil pointer in modelsdk Reader.GetRawUnitByName (receiver 0x0) via layoutCheckBackend/microflowExists while building a create or modify after a drop; no rollback, the drop and all earlier statements stayed written.
cause: The statement outlasted the 5m per-statement limit. Execute returned the timeout but its goroutine kept running (handlers are not context-aware); runScriptAtomically called exec.Close() (Disconnect sets reader=nil) before Rollback; the abandoned goroutine read the nil reader and its unrecovered panic killed the process before Rollback and before the timeout error was printed.
file: mdl/executor/executor.go (Execute: running WaitGroup + executeRecovered; Close waits abandonedStatementWait)
insight: The stack's goroutine was the one Execute spawns, and nothing else nils the reader mid-statement — that pointed at a timeout, though the report never mentions one: the timeout message is printed after the rollback, which the panic skipped. Reproduced with slowImplicitRebuilds + exec.Close(). Why the statement took 5 minutes: GetRawUnitByName re-decodes every unit of the type per call, once per distinct call target.
